name: AI Homework & Math Solver
intro: Where the photo reads and the answer is correct and shown step by step, and where the solution is wrong and the answer is bare.

apps.title: Studdy: AI Tutor & Math Solver
apps.verdict: Its strength is explaining step by step instead of just handing over an answer, and many say they genuinely started to understand the material and prepared for a test. The weak spot is accuracy: it sometimes gives a wrong answer and you have to regenerate a few times, and the constant asking whether you liked the response is annoying. They also cut the number of free tries.
apps.loved: Step-by-step breakdowns that teach understanding, a personal-tutor feel, test prep, Algebra I help
apps.weak: Sometimes a wrong answer and you have to regenerate, nagging asking whether you liked the response, fewer free tries, a separate subscription for the web version
apps.whoFor: Students who want to understand a topic and prep for tests with step-by-step explanations

quotes.text: Studdy is like a personal tutor and takes you step by step through it h everything in an engaging format.

apps.title: Symbolab - AI Math Solver App
apps.verdict: People value the clear step-by-step explanations and graphing, and many say they finally understand the material. It breaks down on higher math: complex integrals and some Calc 2 problems aren't supported, answers are sometimes wrong, and the camera doesn't always read the problem. A separate frustration is that the useful practice section from the website is missing in the app.
apps.loved: Clear step-by-step explanations, graphing, algebra help, the feeling of actually understanding the material
apps.weak: Struggles with hard integrals and some Calc 2 problems, occasionally gives wrong answers, camera doesn't always read the problem, no proper iPad keyboard, practice section only on the website
apps.whoFor: Students working on algebra and basic courses who want to understand the steps, not just get an answer

apps.title: MathGPT - AI Math Solver
apps.verdict: Its strength is detailed explanations and short video breakdowns of topics, helping people prep for tests and review material after university. But it consistently fails geometry, roughly a third of problems come back wrong, and formulas sometimes render broken as 'frac5/'. The sticky scroll and lack of a proper iPad version also annoy users.
apps.loved: Detailed explanations, video topic breakdowns, custom practice problems per topic, help with exams and review
apps.weak: Struggles with geometry, about a third of answers wrong, broken formula rendering, sticky scrolling, no iPad version
apps.whoFor: Students who need algebra walkthroughs and video topic explanations, but not for geometry

apps.title: Homework Helper: Scan & solve
apps.verdict: Kids love how simple it is: snap the question, get a breakdown, and it genuinely lifts their grades. It breaks on money: the promised free use hits a 3-try wall then demands a subscription, and some people report charges even after cancelling the trial.
apps.loved: Simple photo capture, fast answers, helps raise grades, clear explanations
apps.weak: Hits the paywall fast, too few free tries, charges after trial cancellation, sometimes unhelpful
apps.whoFor: Elementary and middle school students who need a quick photo-based problem breakdown

quotes.text: This is really good it’s not like other ones there for higher grades I had problems with the others ones except for this it’s simple take a picture post it poof all my stuff pops up

apps.title: Maple Calculator: Math Solver
apps.verdict: As a graphing-calculator replacement it's strong: it offers adjustable step depth and handles algebra well. The main pain is input on iPad: no landscape or Split View, so you have to rotate the tablet, and the system keyboard with no spacebar or symbols is a struggle for entering formulas.
apps.loved: Step-by-step solutions with adjustable depth, works like a graphing calculator, good for algebra, useful for students and educators
apps.weak: No iPad landscape mode, awkward system keyboard missing key symbols, loses history on restart, occasionally wrong answers
apps.whoFor: Algebra and higher-math students who work mostly from a phone

apps.title: AI Tutor - Professor Curious
apps.verdict: For AP, SAT and IB prep it's genuinely praised: mock exams, the Questt question bank and topic breakdowns help students feel more confident before the test. It breaks on small learning frictions: the Duolingo-style locked sections get in the way of jumping to the topics you need, and the AI sometimes marks a correct answer wrong and takes away hearts.
apps.loved: AP, SAT and IB prep, mock exams and the Questt question bank, topic breakdowns, responsive support
apps.weak: Duolingo-style locked sections hinder studying, AI marks correct answers wrong, flood of notifications, only sample after paying
apps.whoFor: High schoolers and students preparing for AP, SAT or IB

apps.title: Gauth: AI Study Companion
apps.verdict: People value the clear step-by-step breakdowns and help across many subjects, and some genuinely raised their math grades over the summer. But accuracy is inconsistent, it often gets geometry and graphs wrong, and the ads, constant Plus upsells and connection drops are irritating.
apps.loved: Clear step-by-step explanations, help across many subjects, genuinely raises math grades
apps.weak: Wrong answers on geometry and graphs, pushy ads and Plus prompts, connection failures while scanning
apps.whoFor: Students who need homework help in math and other subjects with a step-by-step walkthrough

quotes.text: I haven’t tried it with any other subjects but they do offer help with history, biology, physics, chemistry, economics,

apps.title: Ai Homework Helper: Scan Solve
apps.verdict: People praise it for giving step-by-step answers with charts and not demanding money on the first screen. But you only get a couple of free tries, then everything is locked behind payment with no daily reset, and that's the main complaint. Accuracy wobbles: reviews say it confuses fractions and stubbornly repeats one wrong answer, in one case leading to a failed quiz.
apps.loved: Step-by-step answers with charts, doesn't ask for payment right away, simple to use
apps.weak: Only a couple of free questions before a hard payment wall, limit on photos, confuses fractions, repeats a wrong answer
apps.whoFor: People who want a quick look at a solution and are willing to pay for ongoing use

quotes.text: I really like how this app doesn’t immediately force me to pay for a subscription and helps me understand what the questions really mean.

apps.title: Sovi.AI - AI Study Companion
apps.verdict: Users value the mode that teaches first and gives the answer after, short clear explanations, and help with last-minute assignments across subjects. But it often errs on math and geometry (one user's sister got an F after double-checking), the app freezes, crashes, and sometimes shows a black screen instead of the photo. Explanations also leak discarded wrong steps like 'wait not right'.
apps.loved: Teach-first-then-answer mode, short clear explanations, help across subjects, feels like talking to a friend
apps.weak: Errors in math and geometry, freezing and crashes, black screen instead of photo, junk steps in explanations, paywall on photo uploads
apps.whoFor: Students who want both to understand a topic and finish a last-minute humanities assignment

quotes.text: My little sister got a F on her homework because I wanted to see if it was right and it wasn’t so 1/10 please find a different app

apps.title: Answer.AI - Your AI tutor
apps.verdict: It really helps with tests and multiple-choice questions, letting you quickly clear a pile of missed assignments and understand what you were stuck on. The weak spot is that it gets some answers wrong, the question limit runs out fast, and cancelling the subscription or getting a refund becomes a nightmare with silent support.
apps.loved: Helps with tests and multiple-choice questions, clears a lot of assignments fast, explains problems from a photo
apps.weak: Wrong answers on some assignments, question limit runs out fast, impossible to cancel the subscription, unresponsive support
apps.whoFor: Students who need to quickly clear tests and multiple-choice assignments, especially in an end-of-quarter crunch

quotes.text: I’ve been really sick for the past two weeks I just got back to school and since it’s the end of the quarter I only had three days to finish 40+ assignments I missed this app helped a lot

apps.title: StudyX: AI Homework & Study
apps.verdict: People value that it explains the solution step by step and helps check homework and find where you went wrong, rather than just handing over an answer. But answers are regularly wrong, and for questions with several parts it only answers one part. It used to give free credits, now free access is just one to five problems a day and the rest costs money, which makes long-time users angry.
apps.loved: Explains the solution step by step, helps check homework and find where you went wrong, clear reasoning in the breakdown, saves students time
apps.weak: Answers are often wrong, only answers one part of multi-part questions, the free limit was cut to one to five problems a day, no Arabic language
apps.whoFor: Students who need to check their solution and understand the steps rather than blindly copy an answer

quotes.text: It's handy for checking answers and steps after finishing homework. It helps quickly identify where I went wrong, making corrections easier.

apps.title: Uknow.AI: Homework&Math Solver
apps.verdict: Praised for step-by-step answers, a free video explanation, and coverage of many subjects, and it helped some pull an A. But it often errs on math (users report 'wrong 80% of the time'), is factually stale (thinks it's still 2024, calls Biden president), runs slowly, and pads answers with extra text. Answers run longer than asked and free tries are limited.
apps.loved: Step-by-step answers, free video explanation, coverage across subjects, few ads
apps.weak: Frequent math errors, stale facts, slow performance, overly long answers, few free tries
apps.whoFor: Students who want step-by-step walkthroughs with video and don't need flawless math accuracy

quotes.text: con ai cũng chấm Giống với kết quả của tôi Nhưng lại chấm Sai kết quả của tôi chán app
It gets rhe job done but it beleves that it is still 2024. It said joe biden was present

apps.title: Camera Math Solver - UpStudy
apps.verdict: People like that it shows how to solve rather than just handing over the answer, and it carries them through regular math. It breaks on geometry, where it spits out random wrong numbers, and on ads: there are so many that one review complains about a fake-virus banner, plus free tries run out fast and you hit the coin wall.
apps.loved: Shows the solving steps not just the answer, helps with regular math, simple and easy
apps.weak: Wrong geometry answers, way too many ads including scary banners, few free tries, network errors even on premium
apps.whoFor: Students who want to understand the solution for regular math and don't mind ads

apps.title: Atlas: AI Study Companion
apps.verdict: Its strength is studying from your own class materials, the app builds tests from them and gets praised for attention to detail on every screen. But the mobile version keeps hanging on a black loading screen, and quizzes made on a computer do not carry over to the phone, forcing a rebuild. The Canvas import pulls in old classes from last year, and billing and subscriptions have a life of their own, charging money even after cancellation.
apps.loved: Studying from your own class materials, generates tests relevant to your topics, easiest to use, attention to detail on every screen
apps.weak: The mobile app hangs on a black loading screen, quizzes from the computer do not sync to the phone, the Canvas import pulls in old classes from last year, money is charged even after canceling the subscription, no iPad support
apps.whoFor: Students who want to prepare from their own course materials and build tests from them

apps.title: MathAce: Solve Study Question
apps.verdict: It gives correct step-by-step answers from a photo of the problem, and when it lands, it genuinely helps you understand and finish homework. Ads ruin it: a clip after every photo, on exit and return, for many every half-minute, and that's the unanimous complaint. On top of that, after the ownership change from Gauth, recognition quality dropped and a payment wall appeared.
apps.loved: Correct step-by-step answers from a photo, clear breakdowns, homework and study help
apps.weak: Ads after every photo and on returning to the app, recognition quality dropped after the switch to MathAce, some features moved behind payment
apps.whoFor: People who photograph a problem and can put up with frequent ads for a free answer

apps.title: Photo Math: AI Homework Helper
apps.verdict: Users value that it explains the working, not just the final answer, and some verified calculus steps against an answer key while the function-graph breakdown gets praise. But for many the scanner returns a blurry photo or replies 'can't solve' to an ordinary problem, answers take up to 5 minutes or never appear, and the whole app sits behind a paywall with no free entry. There are also complaints about charges after cancellation.
apps.loved: Explains the working, function-graph breakdown, reliable calculus steps for some users
apps.weak: Blurry scanner and refusing simple problems, answers taking up to 5 minutes or never, everything behind a paywall with no free entry, charges after cancellation
apps.whoFor: Math students willing to pay upfront for a worked-out solution rather than just the answer

quotes.text: Compared the calculus solutions to my textbook answer key and the steps were completely spot on.

apps.title: SnapMath - Photo Word Math
apps.verdict: For algebra and step-by-step solutions it genuinely helps and explains, which even the 'cheating' crowd appreciates. It breaks on reliability: it can spit out up to 18 different answers for one problem, doesn't handle word equations, and you have to close and reopen the app every time to move to the next question.
apps.loved: Step-by-step algebra explanations, helps understand the problem, has a free mode, handy for people with disabilities
apps.weak: Different answers for one problem, wrong on tests, no word equations, must restart for a new question, paywall after a couple of problems
apps.whoFor: Algebra students who care about step-by-step explanations, not just the answer

apps.title: Quiz AI: AI Homework Helper
apps.verdict: When it works, it gives accurate answers with explanations and saves hours of homework. But accuracy wobbles, and the main trouble is billing: people are promised 4.99 and charged 59.99, a purchased yearly plan stops working, and there's no support. Also, you get only two free solves before a wall, and premium is sometimes limited to math only.
apps.loved: Accurate answers with explanations, saves hours of homework, clear breakdowns, easy to use
apps.weak: Charged more than promised, a purchased yearly plan stops working, no support, only two free solves, premium sometimes math-only
apps.whoFor: Students who need quick homework help and are willing to risk the billing

apps.title: MathSnap: AI Math Solver
apps.verdict: For algebra and simple math it helps, and some people prefer it over Photomath because it explains solutions. It breaks on geometry and formula accuracy, and the free tries burn out fast: 'energy' is spent on every problem and without premium you get cut off.
apps.loved: Helps with algebra and simple math, explains solutions, some prefer it over Photomath
apps.weak: Weak geometry and formulas, occasionally wrong answers, free tries run out very fast, pushy premium prompts
apps.whoFor: Algebra and basic-math students who need a walkthrough of simple problems

quotes.text: This is a very predatory app, not recommended especially if you have a lot of work to do you use energy every time you solve the problem so if you do not buy their premium, you will eventually get cut off

apps.title: Pic Answer - AI Solver
apps.verdict: Many value detailed explanations with examples and coverage beyond math into history and ELA, and it genuinely lifted some grades. But after a recent update it turned slow (up to 30 seconds per answer), answers are often wrong, and users say the 'math' button broke. It also crops photos and hides part of the explanation text, and hits limits despite an 'unlimited free' label.
apps.loved: Detailed explanations with examples, history and ELA coverage, help understanding topics
apps.weak: Slow answers after the update, frequent errors, broken math button, cropped photos and text, limits despite an 'unlimited' label
apps.whoFor: Students who want humanities explanations and simpler math, with patience for the speed

quotes.text: I’ll take a really good non blurry picture and it will still switch up the numbers the cameras blurry, and it will explain it but the words will be blocked off!!
I trusted this app with my work and my grade dropped because of it. Answers are always wrong and they never answer simple questions.
I’m writing this review because, I’m also struggling in reading. Some other people are also struggling in other subjects too. This app needs more subjects

apps.title: Quizard AI: Homework Helper
apps.verdict: When it works it gives a correct answer and explains the steps, and someone passed chemistry with an A all year using it. But it only works half the time, the photo captures the problem incompletely and changes the crop, some answers are wrong, and the free tokens run out fast so you end up moving to Pro.
apps.loved: Gives correct answers and explains the working, helps pass chemistry, fast when it is stable
apps.weak: Works only half the time, photo captures the problem incompletely and re-crops it, some answers wrong, free tokens run out fast
apps.whoFor: Students checking and working through math and chemistry problems, if they will pay for Pro to get tokens

quotes.text: This app is great but after a while you need more tokens and have to get pro. It’s really annoying because I need to do my school work and it’s not letting me ask it questions. Fix that and it’ll be perfect!

apps.title: Math problem solver, photo
apps.verdict: It helps solve and check answers, and the step-by-step breakdown genuinely teaches the method, which is what younger students praise. But the handwriting input barely recognizes what you write, there is no decimal point or fractions, and you cannot enter a variable other than x, y, z. Photo recognition is advertised, but the camera is locked behind payment, and even after paying the accuracy still limps.
apps.loved: Solves and lets you check your own answers, the step-by-step breakdown teaches the method, good for younger students doing addition and subtraction, easy to use
apps.weak: Handwriting input barely recognizes what you write, no decimal point or fractions, you cannot enter a variable other than x, y, z, camera recognition is paid only, does not solve word problems
apps.whoFor: Schoolchildren doing basic math who are fine entering problems by hand and skipping the camera

apps.title: Solvo: AI Homework Helper
apps.verdict: People value the step-by-step breakdown and the essay and summary generator, and for some it genuinely rescued their math. But accuracy is shaky (users report 6/10 or 85% correct), the app freezes and crashes with a 'Solvo could not generate an answer' error, and the free tier gives only two questions. Billing is a separate pain: charges after cancellation and inside the seven-day window.
apps.loved: Step-by-step problem breakdown, essay and summary generator, help across school subjects
apps.weak: Wrong answers, freezing and crashes, only 2 free questions, limits even on the paid plan, charges after cancellation
apps.whoFor: High schoolers who need step-by-step explanations and are willing to pay while double-checking answers

quotes.text: It does really good answering questions. Not always right but about 85 percent right
It’s alll good intel it tells me that i have no more things for my problems, i thought that it was like just normal, so i kept trying to take pictures but it wasn’t letting me
I’m in class and I’m so cooked and this app not helping

apps.title: Math AI Homework Helper,Solver
apps.verdict: It gives a clear step-by-step breakdown, handles even some higher math, and explains rather than just handing over the answer. It breaks down on the fact that much is locked behind a paid subscription and it demands money right away, the camera does not work for some users, and the one-scan-per-30-minutes limit stops you re-shooting a bad frame.
apps.loved: Clear step-by-step breakdown, handles even some higher math, explains rather than just giving the answer
apps.weak: Much locked behind a paid subscription and demands money immediately, camera fails for some users, one-scan-per-30-minutes limit
apps.whoFor: Students who want a step-by-step breakdown of math problems up through some higher math, if they will pay and tolerate the scan limit

apps.title: MathMaster: Math Solver & Help
apps.verdict: Real human experts solve the problems inside, and when they land it, the answer is correct with a step-by-step explanation and decent speed. The problem is inconsistency: roughly one in ten answers is wrong, the paid priority queue doesn't speed things up, and the cost bites, up to a hundred dollars in a single week. Many are put off that no answer is shown at all without paying.
apps.loved: Live experts give a correct answer with a breakdown, decent response speed, step-by-step explanations, graphing
apps.weak: Roughly one in ten answers is wrong, the paid priority queue doesn't speed things up, very expensive, no answer shown without paying
apps.whoFor: People willing to pay for a breakdown from a real person and tolerate occasional misses

quotes.text: The math experts here actually do help and solve questions and the response time is pretty good. 9/10 times they’ll get the correct answer but they do mess up sometimes. Do no pay for the priority queue it’s a waste of money

apps.title: PhotoSolve: AI Homework Helper
apps.verdict: For some it helps them absorb math and chemistry better and the clear explanations get praise. But in practice accuracy is around 70%, the app closes on its own, and after an update answers take 10+ minutes while the phone drops out. The free tier gives only 3-5 scans a day, and there are complaints about charges months after cancellation.
apps.loved: Clear explanations, help with chemistry and math, a sense of progress for some users
apps.weak: Around 70% accuracy, self-closing crashes, 10+ minute answers after the update, only 3-5 scans a day free, charges after cancellation
apps.whoFor: Chemistry and math students willing to pay and tolerate a daily scan limit

apps.title: Photomath
apps.verdict: It used to catch the problem instantly from a photo and show the working, and that is what people loved. The main pain now is that from a photo it swaps in a similar but wrong problem with a different answer, and it cannot handle high school or college level math, often bouncing you to Google.
apps.loved: Shows the working not just the answer, handles simple math well, handy for copying on a test
apps.weak: Swaps in a wrong problem with a different answer from a photo, fails at complex math, redirects to Google instead of solving
apps.whoFor: Students needing simple problems with the working shown, not for hard high school or college math

quotes.text: I take a picture of a question with all the answers included and it pops up a picture of a different question with different answer ch

apps.title: Nerd AI - Math Problem Solver
apps.verdict: It explains the working clearly and neatly and is fine for checking basic homework, with some STEM students using it to verify formulas and biology answers. But accuracy wobbles, it gives different wrong answers to the same question, it freezes even for paying users, and the lifetime purchase is tied to one device and vanishes when you switch phones.
apps.loved: Explains the working clearly, good for checking basic homework, verifies formulas and biology answers
apps.weak: Wobbly accuracy giving different wrong answers to the same question, freezes even for paying users, lifetime purchase tied to a device and lost on switch
apps.whoFor: Students checking basic homework and STEM formulas, as long as they do not count on the lifetime purchase across devices

apps.title: PhotoMath Solver AI: MathBox
apps.verdict: Some users are happy with the college algebra help and the clear layout. But there are many complaints about wrong answers (a simple 7k-3k example solved incorrectly), no steps shown after paying, and the subscription asking for money again even after purchase. The camera often won't take the photo, and the built-in SAT questions are broken.
apps.loved: College algebra help, clean and clear layout, helps when math just isn't clicking
apps.weak: Wrong answers even on simple problems, payment doesn't unlock steps, subscription asks for money again, camera often won't take the photo, broken SAT questions
apps.whoFor: People who need an answer on basic algebra and can tolerate misses

quotes.text: When I was doing homework i was looking for the steps to find it, but it doesn’t give you the steps and just gives the solution, which isn’t helpful when I'm doing math.

apps.title: Numerade - Homework Help
apps.verdict: The core value is video solutions to textbook problems, and when they are there people genuinely learn the method. But the videos are often cut off at the edges with no zoom, so half the steps are invisible, and a link from Google opens the app without the problem you wanted. On top of that many people are stuck trying to cancel, there is no cancel button in the app or on the site, and free trials rack up large charges with no warning.
apps.loved: Video solutions to textbook problems help you understand the method, step-by-step breakdown, raises grades, the AI gives explanations on request
apps.weak: Videos and steps are cut off at the edges with no zoom, a Google link opens the app without the problem you wanted, canceling the subscription cannot be completed, AI answers are often wrong, the app freezes and glitches
apps.whoFor: Students who need video walkthroughs of problems from their specific textbook

apps.title: Homework AI - Math Helper
apps.verdict: For some it helps them understand material and lift their grades, especially when studying late after sports. But mostly people arrive as a Gauth replacement and get let down: the scanner replies 'I can't directly view photos', botches even 10÷2, payment kicks in after three questions, and charges continue after cancellation. It also lacks Arabic in translation.
apps.loved: Helps understand material and improve grades, handy late at night
apps.weak: Scanner won't read photos, gross errors in simple math, payment after 3 questions, charges after cancellation, no Arabic
apps.whoFor: Students looking for a Gauth replacement who can tolerate errors and an early paywall

apps.title: Course Hero: AI Homework Help
apps.verdict: It helps you check your work against other people's solutions for course materials and format papers, and most of the time the answers are right. But the model of limited document unlocks on top of a paid subscription frustrates people most, plus the camera catches the problem only half the time, answers sometimes load for 20 minutes, and cancelling is nearly impossible.
apps.loved: Helps check work against others' solutions for course materials, format papers, mostly correct answers
apps.weak: Limited document unlocks despite a paid subscription, camera catches the problem only half the time, answers load for 20 minutes, nearly impossible to cancel
apps.whoFor: Students who need to check solutions against course materials and format papers, if they can live with the unlock limit

apps.title: bartleby: Math Homework Helper
apps.verdict: The human-expert model delivers a quality answer when everything works, and it helps people across subjects. But answers can take hours (users report 2-3 hours), experts reply in illegible handwriting, the app crashes, rejects correct passwords, and glitches on iPad and web. A separate pain: monthly charges after cancellation with no reminder at all.
apps.loved: Quality answers from human experts, coverage of any academic question, essay library
apps.weak: 2-3 hour waits for an answer, unreadable handwriting, crashes and login failures, iPad and web glitches, charges after cancellation with no reminders
apps.whoFor: Students who want a real expert's walkthrough and can wait hours rather than needing it instantly

quotes.text: Some of these “experts” have the sloppiest handwriting. I would never turn something in to my professo

apps.title: Math Solver AI Homework Helper
apps.verdict: People value the live experts who walk through a problem step by step and pull students through statistics, which helped some pass their class. But paying users widely report that after payment the app stops granting access or says 'can't read the photo', charges keep coming, and cancelling the subscription or getting a refund is nearly impossible.
apps.loved: Live experts explain step by step, helps pass statistics, logical problem breakdowns
apps.weak: Loses access after payment, often can't read the problem photo, wrong answers, impossible to cancel subscription or refund
apps.whoFor: Students who want a real human walkthrough and can stomach the billing risk

quotes.text: I like that it explains the logic behind the solutions instead of just giving the final answer. It’s been a consistent tool for better understanding algebraic concepts.
The experts are friendly and very helpful. This helped me get through elementary statistics.

apps.title: Calculator 17 - Math Solver
apps.verdict: People install it for the on-screen calculator widget that Apple does not offer, but the widget lags and trails keystrokes by a couple of seconds. Cut-off buttons, portrait-only layout on iPad, and rounding that turns 3.5x1.5 into 5.2 instead of 5.25 wear people down. Inside the app itself math is fast, and that is what keeps it around.
apps.loved: Fast math inside the app itself, an on-screen calculator widget Apple does not offer, simple and easy interface, free
apps.weak: The widget trails keystrokes by a couple of seconds, buttons and operators run off the screen edge, iPad works only in portrait, answers get rounded incorrectly, the widget sometimes shows up blank
apps.whoFor: People who just want a simple calculator widget on iPhone and can live with input lag

apps.title: Socratic AI - Homework Helper
apps.verdict: When it works, it helps you understand a topic and gives an answer, and long-time users say they got through school and college on it. But right now it's unreliable: constant timeouts and unknown error, streaks of wrong answers in a row, and weak step explanations. People remember it used to be free with ads, and now there's a payment wall after a couple of questions and a three-a-day limit.
apps.loved: Helps you understand a topic, carries you across many subjects, simple for beginners and older users
apps.weak: Frequent timeouts and unknown error, streaks of wrong answers in a row, weak step explanations, payment wall after a couple of questions and a three-a-day limit
apps.whoFor: People who need a one-off hint on a topic and can live with instability and limits

quotes.text: it didn’t do the best job at explaining the steps. That’s really my only complaint right now but yeah I wish it could just explain the steps better because it could help you way better to be able to actually learn

apps.title: MathGPT Math Solver & Homework
apps.verdict: When it works, people like the simplicity: snap the problem, get a detailed answer, with coverage from physics to English. But a huge share report the app throwing an error on every scan for weeks or stopping right after they paid, plus ads remaining even after purchase.
apps.loved: Simple photo capture, detailed answers, coverage from math to physics and English
apps.weak: Constant scan errors for weeks, stops working after payment, ads even after buying, no refunds or support
apps.whoFor: People who want a quick photo breakdown across subjects and get lucky with a working build

apps.title: AnswersAi - Snap & Solve
apps.verdict: People grab it to check their answers, but it gets things wrong more often than it helps: students report failing quizzes and tests after trusting it. A separate pain is that the subscription is nearly impossible to cancel and charges keep coming while support goes silent.
apps.loved: Sometimes helps college students pass classes, saved a semester for a few
apps.weak: Frequently wrong answers, fails quizzes and tests, slow and freezes, can't cancel subscription, unexpected charges
apps.whoFor: University students willing to double-check every answer and fight through cancellation hassle

We do the work and then snap it on here to check and have to change our answers, she has failed a few tests do to this!!!

apps.title: Calculator Air: AI Math Solver
apps.verdict: It is basically a regular calculator with photo formula recognition and currency conversion, but the key AI features are locked behind a 10 dollar a week subscription, which is absurdly expensive for a calculator. People are annoyed by the constant do you like the app prompt, pushy ads and the camera not solving anything for some users.
apps.loved: Recognizes formulas from a photo, converts currencies and does square roots, clean design
apps.weak: 10 dollar a week subscription on a calculator, nagging do you like the app prompt, lots of ads, camera fails to solve problems
apps.whoFor: People who want a simple calculator with photo recognition, if they can put up with the pricey subscription and ads

apps.title: Quiz AI: Homework Helper
apps.verdict: A few users praise the clear explanations and say they got through their studies on it. But the core of the complaints is billing and login: even after paying, it kicks you out and demands a subscription again after two or three questions, forcing a delete-and-reinstall. On top of that, it charges after cancellation, access is lost when you switch phones, and it's useless beyond basic algebra.
apps.loved: Clear explanations, helps carry you through your studies, breaks a problem down step by step when it works
apps.weak: Kicks you out and demands a subscription again after paying, charges after cancellation, access lost when switching phones, useless beyond basic algebra
apps.whoFor: People who need help with basic algebra and are willing to risk the billing and login trouble

quotes.text: The app will not complete more than 2 questions for me before I keeps asking me to renew my subscription which I already did. I have to delete and re download the app after every 3 questions which is extremely inconvenient.

apps.title: Goth AI - Math Problem Solver
apps.verdict: It's billed as a photo solver, but people widely complain that answers are wrong even after buying premium. On top of that, ads rain down on nearly every action along with pop-ups, and you only get a couple of free tries before it demands payment.
apps.loved: Sometimes accurate answers, helps with simple math and spelling
apps.weak: Often wrong answers even after paying, flood of ads and pop-ups, only 2-3 free tries, photo input broke after an update
apps.whoFor: At most for simple school math, and even then with double-checking

apps.title: Stealth AI - Study Companion
apps.verdict: People use it to humanize AI text for essays and for the photo solver, and when it works they turn in last-minute work and pass detectors. But the app regularly fails to show answers after a scan, throws a fetch error, and simply does not respond, and it flags its own humanized text as "95% AI". Billing is a separate irritant, charging 9.99 or 24.99 with no intent to renew, cancellation that fails for months, and a subscription that does not activate after payment.
apps.loved: Humanizes AI text to slip past detectors, bails you out with last-minute essays, the photo solver gives fast answers, there is a study simulator
apps.weak: Often fails to show answers and throws a fetch error, flags its own humanized text as 95% AI, gives wrong answers, charges money with no intent to renew, canceling the subscription fails for months
apps.whoFor: Students who need to rush an essay in and run text past detectors, if they can stomach the failures and the billing

apps.title: homie AI: Math Photo Solver
apps.verdict: It is meant as a photo math solver, but answers come back in other languages, Spanish, French, Russian, that people cannot read, which breaks the whole point. Accuracy limps, and it often refuses chemistry and biology that it advertises, even though it used to help. Billing finishes people off, charging 4.99 every week with no visible plan in the account, and after a yearly payment the app stops working entirely.
apps.loved: Helps double-check your own work with no lag, gives correct answers when it works, bails you out with math
apps.weak: Answers come back in other languages, Spanish French Russian, that you cannot read, accuracy limps, refuses to solve chemistry and biology though they are advertised, only three problems a day for free, charges 4.99 every week
apps.whoFor: People who need to quickly double-check math and are willing to gamble on the answer language and the billing

quotes.text: I cannot say enough about this app! It allows me to double check my work and rarely has any lags or misunderstandings!
The app now keeps giving me answers in foreign languages that aren’t english and I can’t understand the answer because I can’t read it

apps.title: PopAi: AI Chat&Homework Helper
apps.verdict: It is meant as an AI helper for chat and homework, but detailed reviews say the video and generator are weak and the presentations come out dull with random pictures. Feeding a slide deck from a PC leaves the app stuck in a loop demanding an upgrade. A separate mess is canceling the subscription, it charges 14.99 with no clear warning, and support runs you in circles and will not let you cancel.
apps.loved: Fast and responsive support per the real reviews, an early entry into AI toolboxes, some long-term subscribers of several years
apps.weak: The video and image generator are weak, presentations are dull with random photos, the PC login gets stuck in an upgrade loop, it charges 14.99 with no clear warning, canceling the subscription is nearly impossible
apps.whoFor: People who want one AI toolbox for chat and rough presentations and are willing to fight the billing

apps.title: Chegg Study - Homework Help
apps.verdict: It used to be a place where real experts helped you work through problems and that saved people in college. Now AI answers instead of experts and it is often wrong, while the 20 dollar a month plan either fails to load an answer or just shows similar questions from its database instead of yours. Add complaints about being signed out on a second device and charges after cancelling.
apps.loved: Sometimes explains the working better than a professor, used to have real experts answering
apps.weak: Experts replaced by an error-prone AI, answers often fail to load, shows similar questions instead of yours, signs you out on a second device, charges after cancellation
apps.whoFor: Almost no one as it stands now, at most for ready answers from the database if you are lucky enough to find your question

quotes.text: They got rid of the ask an expert feature so now it is all terrible AI. The AI cannot answer any questions. There was no notice that they got rid of the ask an

apps.title: Answer App - Coursology AI
apps.verdict: A few happy users say it got them through courses like paramedic school and that the owl chat is handy. But the overwhelming majority report consistently wrong answers, broken features, an app and web version that don't share the same account, and crashes that wipe progress. There are also many complaints about non-refundable charges and a hidden cancel button.
apps.loved: Owl assistant chat, fast answers for some users
apps.weak: Frequently wrong answers, broken features, app and web don't sync, crashes wiping progress, non-refundable charges and hidden cancel
apps.whoFor: Realistically no one reliably, at most trying the chat helper while ready to cancel immediately

apps.title: FastMath - Take Photo & Solve
apps.verdict: Hardly anyone gets value out of it for free because after you scan, the solution is shown blurred and you must pay per answer. Many complain the answers are wrong even when paid, there are no correct steps, it does not solve word problems, and sometimes it just stops working.
apps.loved: Sometimes helps with basic math problems, handy for a couple of siblings to share
apps.weak: Solution shown blurred and locked behind pay-per-answer, wrong answers even when paid, no correct steps, cannot solve word problems, stops working
apps.whoFor: Almost no one, at most for the simplest problems if you are willing to pay per answer

apps.title: Algebra Math Solver
apps.verdict: The rare happy users say it helps with math anxiety and gives accurate answers, and one praises it for handling imaginary numbers. But the overwhelming majority hit a hard payment wall: not a single free answer, double and repeated monthly charges, no way to cancel or delete, and only an answer with no steps. Problem recognition is sluggish and often won't load.
apps.loved: Helps with math anxiety, accurate answers when it works, handles imaginary numbers
apps.weak: No free answers at all, double and repeated charges, can't cancel the subscription or delete, shows the answer with no steps, the problem often won't load
apps.whoFor: Almost no one, except someone who just wants a bare algebra answer and doesn't mind a harsh subscription

quotes.text: For a person who generally experiences anxiety over math this app really helps me to find the answers to problems, thus helping me to understand how to come up with answers
